```python

                   AClass.execute.si("", ""),
                   AClass.execute.si("", "")),
             group(AClass.execute.si("", ""),
```

Unsure but there is a bug around group/chord such that for long canvas the tasks may start before the group/chord has been fully defined. I think there either was a fix on 4.4 or a fix was opened.

I think it's about chord upgrade(I think that feature should be removed for advanced "handmade" DAG, multiple task result reuse), couse group of 3 chained with group of 1 become a chord and something that will be chained after can be parallelized losing the chain structure. It's inconsistent in each case, sometimes you get the chord promote and sometime dosn't.

```
>         task = chain(group(task1.si("1"),
                           task1.si("2"),
                           task1.si("3")),
                     group(task1.si("4"),
                           task1.si("5"),
                           task1.si("6")),
                     group(task1.si("7")),
                     group(task1.si("8"))
                     )
        t = task.delay()
```
still not fixed...prints: 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 7 7 8 8 8
isnt it fixed in new releases?

issue.title: Fixed bug when chaining a chord with a group

body:
> ```
> >         task = chain(group(task1.si("1"),
>                            task1.si("2"),
>                            task1.si("3")),
>                      group(task1.si("4"),
>                            task1.si("5"),
>                            task1.si("6")),
>                      group(task1.si("7")),
>                      group(task1.si("8"))
>                      )
>         t = task.delay()
> ```
> 
> still not fixed...prints: 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 7 7 8 8 8

It appears the bug is caused by chaining a chord with a group where `group(task1.si("7"))` and `group(task1.si("8"))`  were chained to `task1.si("4")`, `task1.si("5")` and `task1.si("6")`, instead of `group(task1.si("7"))` being chained to `group(task1.si("4"),task1.si("5"),task1.si("6"))`, and `group(task1.si("8"))` being chained to `group(task1.si("7"))`, which is why they get executed exactly 3 times instead of only once.
Try adding to the second group for example `task1.si("6b")`, and you'll get 1 2 3 4 5 6 6b 7 7 7 7 8 8 8 8.

This happens when the chain upgrades the groups to chords and attempts to chain the upgraded primitives again, it fails to recognize the upgraded chord which is why it doesn't chain it correctly (a.k.a to the body of the new chord, creating a new chord again in our case). 
I attempted a fix at `chord.__or__()`.

Investigating it, I found that "manually" upgrading the chord reproduces the bug in a different flow!
```python
task = chain(
           chord(
               header=group(task1.si("1"), task1.si("2"), task1.si("3")),
               body=group(task1.si("4"), task1.si("5"), task1.si("6"))
           ),
           group(task1.si("7")),
           group(task1.si("8"))
       )
t = task.delay()
```
Will also cause a similar bug due to similar reasons, but in `chain.__or__()`

@Ixiodor @TauPan I've opened a PR with a possible fix. If there's a way you can test it on your systems as "acceptance tests" (in addition to the new integration tests I've added), it could confirm the fix really worked without hurting anything else (which is hard to know from my perspective) before merging to `master`.

I could quite easily run my testcase from the google groups post but I'm not sure if that's the kind of test you need.

Regarding our application the remote workers are stuck with celery 5.1.2 for now (because of python 3.6 on CentOS) and we'll be able to migrate to a more recent celery release much later to test the real business code.

On the local workers, which I can easily run against #7919, I don't have those kinds of workflows so my testcase is the only option there.

I wasted a lot of hours to debug this problem, before I found this bug report @Nusnus Thanks a lot for taking care of this :hugs: 

WORKAROUND: add dummy task after group (than it is converted into chord correctly)
```
chain(
    group(test_task.si("g1.1", 1), test_task.si("g1.2", 3)),
    group(
        test_task.si("g2.1", 10),
        test_task.si("g2.2", 5),
    ),
    # test_task.si("fix", 1),  <== workaround
    chain(
        test_task.si("duplicated", 1), # executed 2 times (once parent is "g2.1" second time it's "g2.2")
    ),
)()
```
